_meta.purpose: Category membership, crop attributes, curated traits and rooftop/container suitability for the food plants, agricultural crops and urban-garden plants people actually ask PlantDoctor about.
_meta.scope: This file never creates a taxon. Every 'scientific_name' must already resolve to a plant row in the GBIF import, through canonical_name, an existing synonym, or the alias table in name_aliases.json. An unresolvable name fails the build rather than being dropped, so a typo cannot silently shrink the catalogue.
_meta.provenance: Project-curated. Category assignment and siting guidance are compiled from standard Indian agricultural extension and horticultural practice. They are recorded as UNVERIFIED_CATEGORY / UNVERIFIED_ROOFTOP rather than VERIFIED, because no single published work is cited per record. Nothing here is a dosage, a spray recipe, or a safety claim.
_meta.why_unverified: Per-record 'sources' arrays are empty. A record only becomes VERIFIED once a named publication is listed for it. This matches the convention used by pests.json, plantvillage_classes.json and rooftop_greenery.json.
_meta.how_to_verify: For a record, add entries to its 'sources' array citing a named work (title, publisher or institution, year, URL or DOI). Empty 'sources' keeps the record UNVERIFIED and scripts/validate_plants.py will report it as unverified.

field_definitions.categories: Category codes from plant_categories.json. Several may apply; 'primary_category' is the label a browse card shows.
field_definitions.names: Extra names beyond the GBIF vernacular name. 'hi' is the established Hindi name, 'transliterations' are the Latin-script spellings people type, 'variants' are other English forms, and 'taxonomic_synonyms' are real historical or alternate botanical names that must resolve to this same plant.
field_definitions.crop: Agricultural crop attributes: which part is harvested, life cycle, sowing and harvest windows in Indian practice, and typical duration. These drive the crop-information panel.
field_definitions.rooftop: Container and rooftop siting: whether it tolerates a pot, how much sun it needs, water band, minimum container volume, rooting depth, drainage, wind and heat tolerance, and hazards such as toxicity or aggressive roots.
field_definitions.traits: Curated plant characteristics in a key/value form, used for search and for the plant profile. These are horticultural facts, distinct from the GBIF-derived measurements in plant_characteristics.

_meta.safety_rule: Watering and feeding guidance is expressed as bands and soil-moisture checks, never as a measured volume, dilution or spray recipe. Toxicity notes point at the recorded status and never advise ingestion or treatment.
_meta.data_release_notes: Data release 2026.10.1 adds category membership, crop attributes, curated traits and rooftop/container suitability for the food and urban-garden crops.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; rabi September-November; summer February-March in the plains
crop.harvest_period: 1.5-2 months after sowing; pods picked every 2-3 days

traits.value: erect branching 1-2 m with a rough, hairy stem

rooftop.establishment_watering: needs steady water; drought makes the pods tough and stops flowering
rooftop.pruning_requirement: remove lower yellow leaves and pinch once to encourage side shoots
rooftop.special_hazards: The leaves and stems are hairy and can irritate skin.
rooftop.notes: Tolerates heat well and gives a long harvest. Needs a large pot and staking, since a healthy plant reaches well over a metre.

traits.value: erect tuft from a single basal plate

rooftop.drainage: very free draining and loose; bulb must not be disturbed once formed
rooftop.establishment_watering: steady moisture while leaves are growing, then reduce to let the bulb mature
rooftop.pruning_requirement: stop watering about two weeks before harvest
rooftop.notes: Grows acceptably in a deep tub or a row of wide pots. Bulb size stays small in containers, but green onion can be cut all season.

traits.value: erect tuft from a clove-bearing basal plate

rooftop.establishment_watering: even moisture in autumn and winter, then withhold water to size the bulb
rooftop.pruning_requirement: stop watering about two weeks before harvest
rooftop.notes: Performs well in a wide pot or small bed; needs a cold winter period to bulb properly, so it is less reliable in tropical cities.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep the surface damp
rooftop.notes: A common edible on Indian terraces and in cracks of paving; grows happily in a shallow tray.

traits.value: erect to spreading annual up to 2 m

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep moist until established, then let it dry slightly between waterings
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch the tips to encourage branching
rooftop.notes: Grows well in a terrace tub and gives both a leafy harvest and a seed head. Can self-sow freely in a pot.

crop.sowing_season: kharif and rabi, sown throughout the year in mild areas
crop.harvest_period: cut and come again every 3-4 weeks

traits.value: broad ovate to rhomboid, often bronze or purple

rooftop.establishment_watering: water every 2-3 days in summer; it wilts fast in a small pot and recovers quickly
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch tips and shear leaves regularly
rooftop.notes: One of the most productive pot vegetables: it regrows after each cut, tolerates heat, and self-sows.

traits.value: pinnate with four paired obovate leaflets
low bushy plant; flowers above ground, pods bury

rooftop.drainage: very free draining, sandy loam preferred
rooftop.establishment_watering: water consistently until flowering, then keep it on the drier side so pods set
rooftop.notes: Needs a deep, loose medium so the pegs can bury and the pods form underground. Not a hanging-basket plant.

traits.value: erect tufted grass with loose panicle

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; oats dislike drying out
rooftop.notes: An unusual but workable container cereal in a cool season; best in a deep tub rather than a hanging pot.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist
rooftop.notes: Tolerates cooler weather than most vegetables and its leaves are edible too.

traits.value: lower leaves pinnatifid, upper sessile and clasping

rooftop.establishment_watering: water steadily, then reduce once pods form
rooftop.notes: Gives early greens and then seed. Prefers the cooler months; it bolts quickly in peak summer heat.

crop.sowing_season: rabi, sown August-September, planted out October-November

traits.value: large, waxy, blue-green, in a tight head
short stem with a dense rosette of overlapping leaves

rooftop.drainage: firm, free draining, heavily compacted soil
rooftop.establishment_watering: needs steady, generous water; drought makes the head loose and bitter
rooftop.pruning_requirement: remove yellow outer leaves as they appear
rooftop.notes: A heavy, thirsty feeder. It does best in a large terrace tub with steady moisture, and heads stay smaller in containers than in a field.

traits.value: short stem with a compact white curd

rooftop.drainage: very rich, free draining, moisture-retentive soil
rooftop.establishment_watering: never let it dry once the curd starts forming; drought ruins it
rooftop.pruning_requirement: blanch the curd by tying the outer leaves over it once it is about 3 cm across, or the head will green
rooftop.notes: Demanding: rich soil, constant water and a cool season. A rooftop choice only where a deep tub and steady watering are possible.

rooftop.establishment_watering: steady, generous water
rooftop.notes: The heading cabbage variety, held separately because GBIF records it as a variety of Brassica oleracea.

traits.value: erect stem with side flower heads

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist, especially once heads form
rooftop.pruning_requirement: cut the main head just above a side shoot to keep it producing
rooftop.notes: Gives repeat harvests from one plant, which makes it high value in a small rooftop space.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist
rooftop.notes: Hardy in cold weather and quick to harvest.

traits.value: woody perennial shrub, grown as an annual crop

rooftop.establishment_watering: water well in the first season, then sparingly; drought-tolerant once nodulated
rooftop.pruning_requirement: light tip pinching to keep it bushy
rooftop.special_hazards: The dry pod is ornamental but not edible; pods must be cooked before the seed is eaten.
rooftop.notes: Deep rooted and long-cropping, so it needs the largest pot of any rooftop pulse. A north Indian rooftop classic.

traits.value: simple, ovate-lanceolate, entire, glossy dark green

rooftop.drainage: very free draining, warm root zone
rooftop.establishment_watering: water evenly; allow the surface to dry slightly between waterings
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch the first growing tip to force branching; avoid over-pruning once flowering starts
rooftop.special_hazards: The leaves and stems are not edible. Extremely hot varieties should not be eaten raw by people sensitive to capsicin.
rooftop.notes: One of the best rooftop vegetables: compact, heavy-cropping in a 20-litre pot, and it needs less root depth than tomato. Sweet bell types want the most sun; hot chilli types tolerate more heat and less light.

crop.sowing_season: sown in the rainy season, or set out as rooted cuttings

rooftop.establishment_watering: water when the top few centimetres are dry; dislikes wet roots
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch the tip once to bush out, then pick often
rooftop.notes: An evergreen, long-lived, highly productive rooftop chilli that keeps fruiting for years in a sunny pot.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July, sown with the first monsoon rain

traits.value: erect grass with a dense cylindrical candle head

rooftop.establishment_watering: moist until emergence, then almost no water once rooted
rooftop.notes: The most heat- and drought-tolerant of the common millets and a good rooftop cereal in a hot, dry city.

traits.value: pinnately compound with small toothed leaflets

rooftop.establishment_watering: soak-free: water only after the seedling is established, then rarely
rooftop.notes: An excellent balcony crop. Needs only a moderately deep pot, and fixing atmospheric nitrogen means no fertiliser is needed.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; rabi September-November; summer January-February in the plains

traits.value: large, palmately lobed, rough-hairy, on long petioles
trailing vine with tendrils, or a compact bush type

rooftop.drainage: very free draining; roots must breathe
rooftop.establishment_watering: large, thirsty crop; a small pot must be watered at least daily in summer
rooftop.pruning_requirement: guide along a trellis to save space and improve airflow
rooftop.notes: Produces well in a big container or grow bag on a terrace. Compact bush varieties need no trellis and suit a large pot.

rooftop.establishment_watering: heavy feeder and drinker; needs a very large container
rooftop.notes: A field crop. Only realistic in a very large terrace planter with room for a 4 m vine.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; cooler months in the plains

traits.value: large, deeply lobed, rough, on long stalks

rooftop.drainage: rich, very free draining, high fertility
rooftop.establishment_watering: the heaviest water and feeding demand of any common rooftop vegetable
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pick fruit small and often; harvest male flowers in the morning
rooftop.notes: Enormously productive but needs a very large container and constant watering. Less realistic on a small balcony.

traits.value: basal rosette on a swollen taproot

rooftop.drainage: deep, loose, stone-free soil; stones and compaction fork the root
rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; the surface must never crust over
rooftop.pruning_requirement: thin seedlings early to 3-5 cm apart or the roots stay forked and small
rooftop.notes: Needs a container at least 30 cm deep. Forking is nearly always caused by shallow soil or fresh manure, not by the variety.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July, often as a second crop after rice

traits.value: narrow strap-like, arranged in finger-like spikes

rooftop.drainage: free draining but must not dry out hard
rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; it is less drought-tolerant than pearl millet

species.note: Not Brahmi. Brahmi is Bacopa monnieri, a different plant with a different medicinal reputation; this entry deliberately avoids that name to prevent a wrong identification.

rooftop.establishment_watering: never let the surface dry; it wilts in a few hours of heat
rooftop.notes: Needs a permanently damp tray or wick-fed pot. A poor choice for an exposed, drying roof but excellent in a cool balcony water tray.

rooftop.establishment_watering: water regularly; soybean is shallow-rooted and drought-sensitive at pod fill
rooftop.notes: Fixes its own nitrogen and grows well in grow bags, though it needs more root depth than mung or lentil.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; also a rabi crop in the south

traits.value: tall erect 1.5-3.5 m with a single terminal flower head

rooftop.establishment_watering: water deeply at least twice a week in a pot; it wilts readily
rooftop.pruning_requirement: tie the stem as it thickens; wind will snap a tall plant
rooftop.special_hazards: Its height shades everything below it on a small roof.
rooftop.notes: A cheerful rooftop crop but wants a large, deep, firmly staked pot. Dwarf and branching varieties suit containers far better than the tall field type.

rooftop.establishment_watering: even moisture until emergence, then sparse watering
rooftop.notes: Hardy in a container in a cool, bright position; less suited to a hot exposed roof.

crop.sowing_season: slips planted June-July in the kharif

traits.value: prostrate vine rooting at the nodes

rooftop.drainage: deep, very free draining, loose; waterlogging rots the tuber
rooftop.establishment_watering: water well in the first two months, then reduce sharply
rooftop.pruning_requirement: lift or redirect the vines so they do not root into the drain
rooftop.special_hazards: The leaves and raw tuber are not eaten; cook the tuber.
rooftop.notes: Tolerates heat and neglect, but the tuber needs real root depth, so it suits a large fabric grow bag rather than a pot.

traits.value: broad, wavy or curled, in a loose or tight rosette

rooftop.establishment_watering: the single most important factor: a shallow pot dries in hours and lettuce bolts
rooftop.pruning_requirement: harvest whole or pick outer leaves
rooftop.notes: A shallow bowl or window box on a bright balcony is ideal. It bolts in heat and long days, so treat it as a cool-season crop.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; summer January-March in the plains

traits.value: large, soft, heart-shaped to shallowly lobed

rooftop.establishment_watering: large and thirsty; never let a container dry
rooftop.pruning_requirement: needs strong trellis support and frequent picking of the fruit
rooftop.notes: Suits a rooftop trellis well and gives heavy production, but it needs the largest pot of the common gourds.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist until flowering, then reduce
rooftop.notes: Shallow rooted and quick, so it is one of the easiest container pulses.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep damp; it is a shallow-rooted salad crop
rooftop.notes: Harvestable in under three weeks from a shallow tray, which makes it the quickest green on a rooftop.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; summer February-March in the plains

rooftop.establishment_watering: steady water
rooftop.notes: Reliable in summer heat; pick the ridged fruit young or it becomes fibrous and inedible.

crop.edible_part: immature fruit; mature fruit used as a sponge
crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; summer February-March in the plains

rooftop.establishment_watering: steady water
rooftop.notes: Grows well in a warm rooftop trellis. The mature fruit is the vegetable sponge used as a bath sponge.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; summer January-March in the plains

rooftop.pruning_requirement: train on a trellis and pick frequently for continued cropping
rooftop.special_hazards: Bitter gourd belongs to the same family as cucumber and squash; it is a food plant, but its seeds are not edible.

crop.sowing_season: suckers or tissue-culture plants set out at the start of the monsoon

traits.value: enormous, paddle-shaped, torn along the veins
pseudostem of leaf sheaths up to 2-3 m

rooftop.drainage: very free draining and rich; must never be waterlogged
rooftop.establishment_watering: enormous drinker: a fruiting banana in a pot needs water twice a day in summer
rooftop.pruning_requirement: remove dead leaves and, once the bunch is harvested, cut the pseudostem down to the ground and keep one strong sucker
rooftop.special_hazards: Sap stains and irritates skin; keep away from children.
rooftop.notes: Dwarf varieties such as 'Dwarf Cavendish' or the local Mysore and Neythakiran types are the only realistic choice for a rooftop, and they still need a very large container.

traits.value: creeping in shallow running or flowing water

rooftop.drainage: must stay continuously wet; grows in flowing water
rooftop.establishment_watering: never allow the surface to dry; a wick-fed tray or a small water channel suits it
rooftop.notes: A watercress bed or shallow channel on a shaded balcony works; an ordinary dry pot does not.

crop.sowing_season: sown after the monsoon, or rooted cuttings set out in September
crop.harvest_period: cut regularly throughout the warm season

traits.value: annual or short-lived perennial aromatic herb
opposite, ovate, glossy, slightly toothed, strongly aromatic

rooftop.establishment_watering: water when the top centimetre is dry; basil wilts fast in a small pot
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch the growing tip above a leaf pair early, then harvest the top regularly to keep it bushy; remove flower spikes to keep the leaves sweet

rooftop.notes: Very productive in a small pot and it self-sows readily on a terrace. One of the easiest herbs for a balcony kitchen.

crop.sowing_season: propagated by seed or cuttings at the start of the monsoon
crop.harvest_period: harvest leaves year-round in a warm climate

traits.value: opposite, ovate, finely toothed, hairy, strongly aromatic
branching shrub 30-60 cm with purple flower spikes

rooftop.establishment_watering: water in the dry season, less during monsoon; never waterlog
rooftop.pruning_requirement: pinch tips continuously to keep a dense bush
rooftop.special_hazards: Traditional use in Indian medicine is not the same as a demonstrated medical effect; it is not a substitute for care.
rooftop.notes: Grows year-round in a sunny pot in a warm climate, and is widely grown in rooftop and balcony containers for that reason.

crop.sowing_season: kharif transplanting June-July; rabi in irrigated areas

rooftop.drainage: must not stand waterlogged once established
rooftop.establishment_watering: keep the pot continuously moist for the first two weeks
rooftop.notes: Grows well in a wide, deep tub or cut-and-come-again in a waterlogged paddy-style tray, but a dry rooftop pot rarely gives a full crop.

rooftop.establishment_watering: moist until emergence, then sparing
rooftop.notes: Held under this name alongside the accepted Cenchrus americanus; recorded here so either name resolves.

crop.edible_part: pods when young; seed when dry
crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; rabi in mild areas
crop.growth_duration: 50-70 days to pods, 90-110 to dry seed

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; never let the surface dry once flowering starts
rooftop.pruning_requirement: train onto a trellis for climbing types
rooftop.notes: Dwarf bush types need no support and give a crop in about two months in a large pot.

crop.sowing_season: rabi, October-November in the plains; February-March in the hills

traits.value: pinnate with tendrils at the leaf tip

rooftop.establishment_watering: water consistently; drought at flowering blanks the pods
rooftop.pruning_requirement: provide a trellis from the start
rooftop.special_hazards: The seeds of some ornamental sweet-pea relatives are not edible; garden pea pods are.

traits.value: low, mat-forming, stems root at the nodes

rooftop.establishment_watering: water lightly and often; it will rot in a soggy pot
rooftop.notes: Spreads from cuttings almost anywhere, survives a missed watering, and is a common edible on Indian rooftops. Too vigorous for a small hanging basket.

traits.value: basal rosette on a swollen root

rooftop.drainage: loose, free draining, not freshly manured
rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; a dry soil makes the root woody and cracked
rooftop.notes: The fastest reliable rooftop crop: some varieties are harvestable in under a month, which makes it ideal for children and for continual succession sowing.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; rabi October in the south

traits.value: lower leaves opposite, upper alternate, lanceolate to oblong

rooftop.establishment_watering: water moderately; overwatering is the main cause of failure
rooftop.notes: A heat-tolerant oilseed that performs well in a terrace tub.

traits.value: erect grass with a dense bristly cylindrical head

rooftop.establishment_watering: moist until emergence, then sparing
rooftop.notes: Short season and modest root depth make it a practical container cereal.

crop.sowing_season: warm season, year-round in frost-free areas

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist
rooftop.notes: Tougher and more heat-tolerant than brinjal, and the leaves are also eaten as a vegetable.

crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July; rabi October-November; summer January-February in the plains
crop.harvest_period: 50 days to first ripe fruit from transplanting

traits.value: odd-pinnate compound, serrated leaflets, hairy and aromatic
bushy or climbing, 0.5-3 m, stems and leaves hairy and strongly scented when crushed

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist every day; inconsistent watering splits the fruit and causes blossom-end rot
rooftop.pruning_requirement: tie to a cane or stake, pinch side shoots, remove leaves below the first flower truss
rooftop.special_hazards: Leaves and stems are not edible and carry solanine; green fruit and cut tomatoes should not be eaten in quantity.

traits.value: large, ovate to lobed, softly hairy, often wavy-edged

rooftop.establishment_watering: needs steady moisture; drought causes tough fruit and bitter fruit
rooftop.pruning_requirement: remove the growing tip after the first fruit to get side branches and more fruit
rooftop.special_hazards: Foliage is hairy and can irritate skin; it is not edible.
rooftop.notes: A heavy feeder with a long season. Warm, sheltered rooftop positions suit it better than exposed ones.

traits.value: deeply lobed, armed with small prickles

rooftop.establishment_watering: light watering; drought tolerant
rooftop.notes: Handles heat, poor soil and neglect, which makes it a reliable rooftop vegetable where finisher crops fail. The prickles are stinging, so put it out of reach of children.

traits.value: upright bushy herb; tubers form on stolons below soil

rooftop.drainage: very free draining and loose; tubers need to swell underground
rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; never let the soil dry once tubers have set
rooftop.pruning_requirement: earth up around the stems as they grow to keep tubers buried and out of the light
rooftop.special_hazards: Green tubers and any green part carry solanine and must not be eaten; the plant foliage is not edible.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep moist for the first three weeks; then drought-tolerant
rooftop.notes: Handles heat, wind and irregular watering better than maize, which makes it the safer rooftop cereal in a hot city.

traits.value: broad ovate to arrowhead, dark green or red

rooftop.pruning_requirement: harvest outer leaves and let the crown regrow
rooftop.notes: Excellent cool-season rooftop crop. Sow little and often, because it bolts fast once days lengthen or temperatures rise.

rooftop.establishment_watering: light frequent watering; a neglected pot is often better for it
rooftop.special_hazards: Some Solanaceae-free but commonly confused with toxic look-alikes; identify by its paired unequal leaves and small pink flowers before eating.

crop.sowing_season: rabi, sown November-December in northern India

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist until emergence, then let the surface dry between waterings
rooftop.notes: Grows in a deep container on a terrace, but the grain head needs more root depth and a cooler winter than most rooftop positions offer.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist
rooftop.notes: Handles a wider range of soils than most pulses and climbs a small support readily.

rooftop.establishment_watering: keep evenly moist; it wilts quickly in a dry pot

crop.edible_part: seed (grain), then whole plant as fodder
crop.sowing_season: kharif June-July, or year-round in mild areas
crop.growth_duration: 90-120 days to green cob; 150-180 to dry grain

traits.value: long, broad, arching, parallel-veined strap leaves
